newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends little changed, thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends little changed, thin trade.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed almost unchanged at 56.87 to the dollar after trading in a tight range of a few local cents, hovering close to the Central Bank's selling rates, dealers said.
The rupee opened at 56.88 against Tuesday's close of 56.90.
"The market was not very liquid," said a foreign bank dealer.

"There were few trade-backed transactions. People are cautious and not willing to create dollar-plus positions because the central bank cap is very close and the upside is very much limited," he said.
Banks were also reluctant to sell dollars as the Central Bank pushed up the U.S. unit in response to its slight gain overnight against the yen, fixing buying and selling rates at 55.9251 and 57.0549.
"The central bank wants to keep the dollar up," said a local bank dealer. "The market can't go above 57.05 because you can buy from the central bank."
The overnight call money rate closed at 15.5 percent after starting at 16 percent.
